# Milestone brief — ui-uplift-m9

**Title:** Land the BAN-R2 policy as a derived test
**Kind:** milestone
**Roadmap:** ui-uplift (plans/ui-uplift/roadmap.yaml)
**Status:** planned
**Lane:** now
**Target:** 2026-08-11 -> 2026-08-20

## Parent epic

- ui-uplift-e2 — Finish debt — every server-emitted class ships with its CSS rule
  Four class families shipped with zero CSS rule anywhere in the stylesheet. The root cause the current-state critic traced nearly every HIGH finding to: feature milestones shipped complete, tested, secure behaviour and left CSS as an afterthought scoped to "does it render", not "does it look finished" — because no milestone's acceptance criteria ever said "style this". This epic closes the backlog AND lands the standing rule as a derived test so it cannot regenerate.

## Summary

UPL-7. Every server-emitted class must have a CSS rule, enforced by a test that derives the check from the on-disk tree rather than a hand-maintained list. Writable here because the fragments are f-strings in server/routes/ — a regex over emitted class literals checked against app.css selectors, with an allow-list for the dynamic status-badge modifier family. A test is the only version of this policy that cannot rot.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Given any class literal emitted by a fragment builder in server/routes/, when the test runs, then it fails unless a matching selector exists in app.css
2. Given the dynamic status-badge modifier family, then the test carries an explicit allow-list rather than false-failing
3. Given a new fragment added later with no CSS rule, when the suite runs, then it fails — the policy binds going forward, not just retroactively
